lines: Summary: "T10 - f5.9, Paramount GTS, SBIG STX-16803, Lodestar SX2 guider with QHY Mini guidescope. LRGB, Ha, OIII, SII"
Observatory: iTelescope.Net at Siding Spring Observatory Australia, MPC Q62
Telescope: T10 0.130m f/7.7 Refractor + reducer + CCD
Timezone UTC +10:00 New South Wales, daylight saving observed
Ops notes: med-wide field astrophotography; Astrodon LRGB, Ha, OIII, SII; raw data at data.itelescope.net; max exposure 1800 s; Bin 1 and Bin 2
CCD: SBIG STX-16803, 16-bit, gain 1.22 e-/ADU, 9 µm pixels, 2.44 arcsec/pixel, cooled -20 C, 4096x4096 (16.8 Mp)
Filters: Astrodon Gen 2 E-Series LRGB, HA3, OIII3, SII3 (3 nm)
FOV 2.77° x 2.77°; orientation up is 359° E of N
Optics: Takahashi TOA-130 apochromatic refractor, 130 mm; reducer Takahashi TOA 645 0.75x; focal length 762 mm f/5.9; guiding QHY Mini guidescope + Lodestar SX2; mount Paramount ME
Horizon angles: N 30, NE 27, E 15, SE 17, S 21, SW 29, W 33, NW 32

workflow: use iTelescope Planning Tool or Telescopius to confirm coordinates/visibility
check framing in Telescopius with correct telescope (else object too small/large)
fill Deep Sky Objects form, RA/Dec most formats, suggested H:M:S and D:M:S (e.g. RA 05:23:25, DEC -10:12:56)
set subs to shortest time giving max S/N
Bias (Bin 1 and 2) and 1800 s darks (Bin 1 and 2) provided as masters, dark scaled with bias
click Acquire images now or Create plan for later (Reservation system)
watch via System Status or View Desktop
tips: short subs reduce bad frames from conditions and cosmic rays
stack many short subs (120 s x 10 vs one 1200 s, only marginally better in theory)
ideal sub lets sky shot noise just exceed dark current
brighter objects shorter subs, darker filters longer, narrowband longer than wideband
match sub times to existing darks
prefer #REPEAT over Qty across filters (4 x LRGB 1200 s without #REPEAT cut at 3/4 gives L,R,G no B
#REPEAT 4 with 1 per filter gives complete sets).
notes: adaptive focus periodically and on temperature change, disabled by #FORCESTARTUP + #NOADAPTIVE.
Limits 1800 s max, 10° min elevation, 45°+ suggested.
Each request produces raw 16-bit FITS, calibrated 16-bit FITS, JPEG preview, optional 16-bit TIFF, optional calibrated FITS to VPhot..
